column3: BSB’s “Bethesda” matches the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Bethzatha” (Βηθζαθά).
BSB follows the critical text without “waiting for the moving of the water” of the Textus Receptus (κίνησιν); “paralyzed” renders a word meaning withered.
BSB omits this verse with the critical text; it appears in the Textus Receptus (“an angel went down at certain times into the pool and stirred the water …,” ἄγγελος).
The Greek describes the man becoming well and walking, while BSB uses “was made well” and “began to walk.”
The critical text leaves the object of “pick up” unstated; BSB supplies “it.”
The Greek uses present “finds”; BSB supplies “the man” for a pronoun.
“Began” is not separately expressed in the Greek imperfect.
The Greek has “that One” for the Father in the latter clause and explicitly adds “likewise.”
The Greek makes their amazement the purpose, “so that you may marvel,” rather than “to your amazement.”
The Greek says he “does not come” into judgment in the present; BSB uses future and replaces “but” with “Indeed.”
The Greek says the hour “is now,” rather than “has now come.”
“Their” before graves is not separately expressed.
“Only” is not separately stated in the Greek hearing clause.
